memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Danielle selected the later Friday American Main Cabin return for this trip because it preserves a comfortable post-summit airport margin. No recurring travel preference was established.

messages.content: I have settled the Atlanta schedule: fly Wednesday evening, attend both Thursday and Friday events, and come home Friday. The East Point visit can wait. Please recheck the sensible nonstop flights and include the full ticket cost and restrictions.

I found two practical Wednesday nonstops from DFW. American leaves at 4:45 p.m. and reaches Atlanta at 7:58 p.m.; Delta leaves at 6:05 p.m. and arrives at 9:12 p.m. Both leave enough time to get downtown and check in that night. Before I calculate the complete totals, will you check a bag, or are you traveling with a carry-on only?
Carry-on only. I will leave it with the hotel Friday morning and collect it after the summit.

That keeps the airfare totals straightforward. The American Main Cabin itinerary is $381.20 round trip: Wednesday 4:45-7:58 p.m., then Friday 5:55-7:22 p.m. The fare includes a carry-on, advance standard-seat selection, and changes without a change fee; a cancellation would produce an airline trip credit rather than a cash refund. The earlier Friday American flight at 4:20 p.m. lowers the fare to $342.20 but compresses the post-summit schedule considerably.

Delta has a $319.20 Basic Economy pairing, Wednesday 6:05-9:12 p.m. and Friday 4:35-6:05 p.m. It includes a carry-on but no advance seat choice, and changes are not allowed. Canceling after the 24-hour grace period would reduce the resulting eCredit by a $99 fee. Delta Main Cabin on the same flights is $389.20 and permits changes, seat selection, and cancellation for an eCredit.
How much usable time do I actually have for the two earlier Friday flights? Assume the summit ends at 1:00 near Centennial Olympic Park.

For American at 4:20, I would leave the summit promptly, walk to the Residence Inn, retrieve the bag, and depart the hotel by about 1:25. A rideshare should reach ATL around 1:50 to 2:10 in ordinary traffic, leaving roughly two hours before departure. That is workable, but a late summit ending or heavy traffic would consume the cushion quickly.

For Delta at 4:35, the same sequence gives another 15 minutes. You would likely have two hours 10 minutes to two hours 30 minutes at the airport. It is viable, though the restrictive Basic Economy terms make its $63 savings over American Main less compelling.
And the 5:55 American? I do not want to spend half the afternoon at the airport, but I also cannot walk out before the summit finishes.

The 5:55 flight is the balanced option. You could stay through a modest overrun, retrieve the bag, and leave downtown around 2:30. Even with a 45-minute drive, you would reach ATL about two hours 40 minutes before departure. If the summit ends on time, you could have a late lunch nearby and still leave the hotel by 2:45 without creating a tight airport margin.
Is the $381.20 truly all-in? No separate charge for the carry-on or choosing a regular aisle seat?

Yes. The $381.20 includes all mandatory taxes and fees, one carry-on, and selection of an available standard Main Cabin seat. Preferred or extra-legroom seats cost more, but there are standard aisle seats available now at no charge. Ground transportation and the hotel are separate.
How does the later Delta option compare? Is there anything after 5:00 that is worth considering?

Delta has a 6:10 p.m. nonstop arriving at DFW at 7:38 p.m. Main Cabin is $417.20 round trip when paired with Wednesday's 6:05 departure. It has terms similar to American Main Cabin: carry-on and standard seat selection included, no change fee, and cancellation to an eCredit. It provides 15 more minutes than American but costs $36 more, while the Wednesday arrival is 74 minutes later. I do not see enough value in that tradeoff.
Agreed. Book the American Main Cabin pair for $381.20, use a no-charge aisle seat on both flights, and do not add insurance or any paid extras.

The American Main Cabin round trip is ticketed for $381.20 under confirmation Q7L9DX. The outbound leaves DFW Wednesday at 4:45 p.m. and arrives in Atlanta at 7:58 p.m.; seat 14C is assigned. The return leaves Atlanta Friday at 5:55 p.m. and arrives at DFW at 7:22 p.m.; seat 16D is assigned. Both are standard aisle seats with no added charge. No insurance, checked bag, or paid extras were added. Changes are allowed without a change fee, subject to fare difference, and cancellation would return the ticket value as an American trip credit. The next unresolved item is the two-night hotel near the summit; its rate still needs to be rechecked and reserved.
